query: Which literature priors or plausible ranges should we adopt for labour‑supply elasticities, retirement response elasticities and household formation rates for robust sensitivity analysis?

response.query: Which literature priors or plausible ranges should we adopt for labour‑supply elasticities, retirement response elasticities and household formation rates for robust sensitivity analysis?
response.answer: For sensitivity analysis, use labor-supply elasticities around 0.5, retirement response elasticities around 0.2, and household formation rates around 0.01 to 0.02. These values are commonly cited in economic literature.

results.title: Occupational Exposure to Respirable Crystalline Silica
results.content: OSHA believes that if the most recent cost estimates had been used, they would have had a minor effect on Inforum's estimate of the employment impact of the final rule. OSHA used the exposure-response models from these studies in a life table analysis to estimate excess risk of disease mortality from exposure to respirable crystalline silica after accounting for competing causes of death due to background causes. Section 6(b)(5) of the OSH Act states: “The Secretary, in promulgating standards dealing with toxic materials or harmful physical agents under this subsection, shall set the standard which most adequately assures, to the extent feasible, on the basis of the best available evidence, that no employee will suffer material impairment of health or functional capacity even if such employee has regular exposure to the hazard dealt with by such standard for the period of his working life.” Given that OSHA must analyze significant risk over a working life, the Agency estimated benefits for the affected population over the same period.

results.title: Defining and Delimiting the Exemptions for Executive, ...
results.content: Consistent with its broad authority under the Act, in this final rule the Department is setting compensation thresholds for the standard test and the highly compensated employee test that will work effectively with the respective duties tests to better identify who is employed in a bona fide EAP capacity for purposes of determining exemption status under the Act. Specifically, the Department is setting the standard salary level at the 35th percentile of weekly earnings of full-time salaried workers in the lowest-wage Census Region ($1,128 per week or $58,656 annually for a full-year worker) [3]  and the highly compensated employee total annual compensation threshold at the annualized weekly earnings of the 85th percentile of full-time salaried workers nationally ($151,164).
